newsitem.title: IRAN: New quake hits Iran, no new casualty reports.
newsitem.headline: New quake hits Iran, no new casualty reports.

text.p: A new earthquake measuring 5.2 on the Richter scale jolted mountainous northwest Iran, only two days after the region's snow-covered towns and villages were devastated by a stronger quake killing at least 554 people.
Iranian radio said on Monday the second quake hit towns and villages around the provincial capital of Ardabil at 10.10 p.m. (1840 GMT) on Sunday. There was no immediate word on casualties.

"According to reports, the tremor and its several aftershocks destroyed some buildings in villages and areas already damaged in the recent earthquake. Power has been cut in most towns and villages," the radio said.
Earlier on Sunday two aftershocks jolted the area, spreading panic among survivors of Friday's quake which measured 5.5 degrees on the Richter scale.
More than 35,000 people in frozen villages and towns have been made homeless by the quake which also injured 2,000 people.

Television footage showed scores of people, most of them crying, gathered around one ambulance carrying 10 bodies, including six children. Graves were being dug and a Moslem cleric was on hand to pray for the dead.
One old man sobbed at the graves of five family members, including his six-year-old grand-daughter. "I had bought her a red dress. Where are you now, Samileh?" he cried.
Officials said although some people might still be buried under the rubble, they did not expect the death toll to rise much beyond the 554 victims accounted for.
"Some bodies are still not discovered...families have lost each other. We are not sure how people can be accounted for," a spokesman for Iran's Red Crescent told Reuters.
"A few more bodies may be lying undiscovered somewhere, but I do not think the death toll will exceed 554 by much," he said.

The radio said 5,000 relief workers, including many volunteers from neighbouring provinces, set up 6,000 tents to shelter thousands of families, who were given blankets, heaters, bread, dates and canned fruit.

The official news agency IRNA said the Iranian cabinet on Sunday earmarked three billion rials ($1 million at the official exchange rate of 3,000 rials to the dollar) for people suffering from the quake.
President Akbar Hashemi Rafsanjani also gave instructions for the "speedy reconstruction of the quake-stricken areas".
Local authorities have announced three days of mourning in the province of Ardabil, which borders the republic of Azerbaijan.
Friday's quake occured 16 hours after a strong tremor jolted Pakistan's Baluchistan province across Iran's southeastern border, killing about 60 people.
Ardabil is an agricultural province inhabited mainly by Iran's Azeri minority. It is one of Iran's coldest regions with freezing temperatures during the winter.
In early February, two earthquakes measuring 6.1 and 5.4 on the Richter scale killed at least 79 people and injured 260 in and around Bojnourd in northeast Iran.
Earthquakes hit Iran regularly. The worst recorded one, measuring 7.3 on the Richter scale, killed 35,000 people in an area near the Caspian coast in 1990.
